authority_treatment.reason: The judgment adopts plaint-only, meaningful full-pleading screening under Rule 11(a)/(d). This is a method, not a finding of pleaded truth or an independent verification of cited precedents.
The court expressly treats substantive tenancy and its term as suitable for civil adjudication; it does not validate the tenancy or decide the distinct District-Court-only objection.
Section 50 applies to the trust-affairs inquiry; Section 51 consent discussion is restricted to suits of that statutory nature, not every trust-tenant suit. No consent facts or misconduct are proved.

Mixed reliefs did not alone warrant whole-plaint rejection. Rule 11 cannot partially reject, and lawful future relinquishment is a separate process; the court restricted continued adjudication to tenancy.
As an evidentiary-role translation it accurately records rival descriptions, without an adjudicated disposition or attributing other tenants' surrender to these plaintiffs.

The court distinguishes the Section 6 settled-possession route from equitable injunction standards, but makes no plaintiff-specific findings satisfying the evidentiary slots. Broader merits computation is not performed.

This narrower research translation directly reflects the restricted continued tenancy issues and the court's explicit choice not to decide forcible possession, with only relevant trial consideration contemplated.

decisive_counterarguments: The trust contended under Order VII Rule 11(a) and (d) that the plaint lacked a real cause of action and that Sections 50, 51 and 80 of the Bombay Public Trusts Act barred ordinary civil adjudication; lower courts accepted rejection (IK-1841885:L69-L76, L80-L82).

Rule 11 also authorizes rejecting a genuinely illusory, manifestly vexatious or legally barred whole plaint; omitted necessary material facts cannot be supplied by particulars (IK-1841885:L103-L105, L119-L126).

Order VII Rule 11 does not allow rejection of only a part of a plaint; Order VI Rule 16 is a different procedure, and giving up reliefs requires appropriate trial-court application subject to Order II consequences (IK-1841885:L105, L117-L118, L131-L132, L137).

The court agreed that prayer D for investigation into trust affairs belongs to Section 50 and, for suits within its class, the Section 51 prior-consent regime; this objection cannot automatically displace the distinct tenancy subject (IK-1841885:L133-L136).

The trust denied forcible eviction, asserted possession was lawfully taken, and invoked voluntary surrender by 22 of 44 tenants; the identities of surrendering tenants, disposal timing and relevance of the interim injunction remain unproved (IK-1841885:L138, L151-L152).

Section 6 permits certain claims by dispossessed settled possessors even without title, whereas equitable injunction against a true owner is subject to different discretionary restrictions; no findings established the plaintiffs' facts under either standard (IK-1841885:L139-L150).

The trust raised arrears, alleged failures to comply with previous writ interim directions, and a District-Court-only jurisdiction objection; their relevance was reserved and the last specific objection was expressly not decided (IK-1841885:L74-L82, L152-L153).
coverage_limits: Model research review of the complete supplied case 1841885 only; neither human gold annotation nor legal approval; no external sources or precedent verification.

All thirty raw premises are assessed as attributed propositions; party-claim TRUE records an assertion, UNKNOWN does not mean FALSE, and CONFLICTED does not establish either speaker's factual version.

All fifty-five enumerated applications and all one hundred fifty predicate mapping candidates are reviewed exactly once. UNUSABLE is limited to wrong slots, incompatible identities/transactions/statuses, missing required bindings, circularity or unsupported upgrades; UNKNOWN conclusions are not negative merits determinations.

R2@1 and R6@1 are OPEN_TEXT; recorded_conclusion TRUE reflects only an explicit bounded target-court assessment with valid inputs, never an independent calculation. R6@2 TRUE is likewise confined to this court's express procedural merits-reservation distinction.

The main tenancy subject (E06), separate trust-affairs prayer (E09), and contested possession event (E10) must remain distinct. E11 identifies unnamed other tenants and cannot be merged with plaintiffs E01.

No authenticated lease, possession records, surrender documents, injunction dates, consent application or payment records are supplied. Neither an 11-year nor 11-month tenancy is established, and no unlawful dispossession, Section 6 recovery or equitable injunction entitlement is decided.

Continuation is restricted by this judgment to tenancy, terms and duration; any forcible-possession plea may be raised and considered only if relevant, and the separate District-Court-only objection has no Supreme Court ruling.
The original precedents are known only as described by the target judgment; legal principles are not asserted to be universally valid outside this jurisdiction, procedural stage or factual framing.
